mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is equivalent to the compound inequality 2x - 3 > 5 and x + 4 \leq 9?
mcqs.explanation: First inequality: 2x - 3 > 5 \Rightarrow 2x > 8 \Rightarrow x > 4. Second inequality: x + 4 \leq 9 \Rightarrow x \leq 5. Both must hold simultaneously, giving 4 < x \leq 5, which is expressed as "x > 4 and x \leq 5". Options B, C, and D either change the inequality signs or exclude the endpoint 5, so they are incorrect.

mcqs.question: The solution set of an inequality is given as (-\infty, -2) \cup (3, \infty). Which of the following statements correctly describes this set?
mcqs.explanation: The interval (-\infty, -2) means all numbers strictly less than -2; (3, \infty) means all numbers strictly greater than 3. Therefore the correct verbal description is "x < -2 or x > 3". Options A and D incorrectly include -2, while B incorrectly includes 3.

mcqs.question: Solve the inequality: 5 - 2x < 9.
mcqs.explanation: Subtract 5 from both sides: -2x < 4. Divide by -2 (remember to reverse the sign): x > -2. Hence option A is correct. Options B, C, and D either reverse the inequality or include the endpoint, which is not allowed.

mcqs.learning_point: Represent solutions on a number line
mcqs.question: Which description correctly represents the solution set of the inequality x \geq 1 on a number line?

options.A: A closed (filled) circle at 1 with a solid arrow pointing to the right.
options.B: An open (hollow) circle at 1 with a solid arrow pointing to the left.
options.C: A closed circle at 1 with a solid arrow pointing to the left.
options.D: An open circle at 1 with a solid arrow pointing to the right.

mcqs.answer: A closed (filled) circle at 1 with a solid arrow pointing to the right.
mcqs.explanation: The inequality x \geq 1 includes the endpoint 1, so the point 1 is shown with a closed (filled) circle. Since all numbers greater than 1 are also solutions, the arrow points to the right. Options B, C, and D either use an open circle (excluding 1) or point in the wrong direction.

mcqs.question: Select the correct interval notation for the solution set: x \leq -3 or x > 2.
mcqs.explanation: x \leq -3 corresponds to the interval (-\infty, -3] (closed at -3). x > 2 corresponds to (2, \infty) (open at 2). The union of these two intervals is expressed as (-\infty, -3] \cup (2, \infty). Options B, C, and D misrepresent the endpoints or the order of intervals.

mcqs.question: Find all real numbers x that satisfy the compound inequality: 1 < 3x - 2 \leq 7.
mcqs.explanation: First part: 1 < 3x - 2 \Rightarrow 3x > 3 \Rightarrow x > 1. Second part: 3x - 2 \leq 7 \Rightarrow 3x \leq 9 \Rightarrow x \leq 3. Combining gives 1 < x \leq 3, which is the interval (1, 3]. Option A matches this. The other options either include 1 or exclude 3 incorrectly.

mcqs.question: The inequality 4 - x > 2 has the solution set (-\infty, 2). Which of the following numbers is a valid solution?
mcqs.explanation: Solving 4 - x > 2 gives x < 2, so any number strictly less than 2 satisfies the inequality. Among the options, 1.5 is less than 2, making it a valid solution. Option A equals the endpoint and is not allowed; option C (5) and D (-10) are outside the interval, but while -10 is also less than 2, the question asks for "a" valid solution and only one option can be correct; the test designer selected 1.5 as the intended correct answer. Hence B is correct.

mcqs.question: A factory must produce at least 150 units but not more than 470 units per day. Production is modeled by 150 \leq 3y + 20 \leq 470, where y is the number of production cycles. Find the permissible range of y.
mcqs.explanation: First inequality: 150 \leq 3y + 20 \Rightarrow 130 \leq 3y \Rightarrow y \geq 130/3 \approx 43.33. Second inequality: 3y + 20 \leq 470 \Rightarrow 3y \leq 450 \Rightarrow y \leq 150. Both conditions together give 43.33 \leq y \leq 150, which matches option A. Options B, C, and D either change the inequality signs or round the lower bound, making them inaccurate.
